readback.name: Poincare.HamiltonScalarGradientQuotientBound.quotient_evolution_le_eight_covRicci
readback.mathematical_statement: For every type M equipped with a Hausdorff topology, charts modeled on real Euclidean three-space, smooth manifold structure with exponent ((top : ENat) : WithTop ENat), compactness, connectedness, a measurable structure satisfying BorelSpace, and second-countable topology, let gt be any family indexed by all real times of smooth Riemannian metrics on M. Fix any real t and x in M. Assume every anchored metric entry is jointly C5 in time and chart coordinates at every pair (s,y) in the real line times M; assume IsClosedNormalizedRicciFlowSolutionAt gt t y for every y; and assume scalar curvature of gt t is strictly positive at every y. The normalized-flow predicate requires that the canonical connection be Levi-Civita at the given y at every real time, and that at time t the derivatives of metric pairings tested against C2 tangent fields satisfy minus twice Ricci plus (2/3) times mean scalar times metric. Put R_s(y) = scalar curvature of gt s at y, S_s(y) = squared norm of its scalar-curvature gradient, A_t(x) = covRicciNormSqAt (gt t) x, the triple metric-orthogonal weighted squared norm of the covariant Ricci derivative, and r_t = the integral of scalar curvature against Riemannian volume divided by total real volume. Then the ordinary time derivative of S_s(x)/R_s(x) at s=t minus the gt t Laplacian of the spatial quotient S_t/R_t at x is at most 8 A_t(x) - (4/3) r_t S_t(x)/R_t(x). The Laplacian is the metric trace of the canonical covariant Hessian and all gradients use the same Riemannian metric as their scalar data. The stated exponent is smooth infinity, not the analytic top exponent. Joint C5 regularity is required at all real times, whereas the flow equation and scalar positivity are required only at the chosen slice. There is no simply-connectedness, positive Ricci curvature, pinching condition, scalar lower bound uniform in time, flow-existence conclusion, or long-time convergence conclusion. The point x supplies nonemptiness. The coefficient 8 and retained normalized coefficient -4/3 are consistent with the exact quotient evolution: writing P = inner(grad R,grad Ricci-norm-squared) and G = inner(grad R,grad S), the nonnegative squares of 2 R times covariant Ricci derivative minus dR tensor Ricci and of R times Hessian of R minus dR tensor dR give 2 R P <= 4 R squared A + S N and R squared H - R G + S squared >= 0, respectively; with R>0 these imply the displayed estimate. This approval concerns the literal assertion and its mathematical consistency, not a claim that its implementation has compiled or that the Poincare conjecture is proved.
